group.passage:
Few inventions are as easy to overlook as the flush toilet. Yet its history shows that a clever device can create a new problem long before it solves an old one.
In the 1590s, the English courtier Sir John Harington described a seat that washed waste away with water, and he built one for Queen Elizabeth I. Nearly two centuries later, in 1775, a Scottish watchmaker named Alexander Cumming received a patent for a design with an S-shaped bend in the pipe. The water that stayed in this bend sealed off the smells rising from the drain, a feature that toilets still rely on today. In 1778 Joseph Bramah patented an improved model worked by a handle, and by 1797 he had sold more than 6,000 of them.
In London, however, the new toilets at first made matters worse. Each flush sent two gallons or more of water into cesspools, the pits beneath houses where waste had long been collected. The pits filled quickly and leaked, and the waste seeped into the wells that supplied drinking water. In 1815 the city first allowed cesspools to be connected to the public sewers, and in 1847 such connections became compulsory. But those sewers had been built to carry rainwater, and they emptied straight into the Thames. Over the century, four outbreaks of cholera killed almost 40,000 Londoners.
The turning point came in the hot, dry summer of 1858, when the river smelled so foul that the period became known as the Great Stink. Members of Parliament could barely stay in their rooms beside the water. Like most people of their time, they believed that diseases spread through bad air rather than dirty water. They were wrong, but their fear made them act. Parliament soon passed a law that let the engineer Joseph Bazalgette begin building a vast network of sewers in January 1859. Huge tunnels running alongside the river caught the waste and carried it east, away from the heart of the city. When cholera returned in 1866, it struck only a district in the east where the system was not yet complete.
The problem Bazalgette tackled has not disappeared everywhere. The chart below shows the share of people using at least basic sanitation, meaning a properly built toilet that is not shared with other households. It is no accident that the United Nations marks World Toilet Day every year on 19 November.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: London built its sewers after scientists proved that dirty water spread cholera.
options.B: An invention can cause new trouble until the systems around it catch up.
options.C: Cholera disappeared from London as soon as flush toilets came into use.
options.D: The Great Stink of 1858 was caused mainly by an unusually hot summer.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the law passed in 1847?

options.A: It ended the cholera outbreaks that had troubled the city.
options.B: It was passed because the Great Stink had frightened lawmakers.
options.C: It required every home in London to install a flush toilet.
options.D: It shifted the city's waste problem from homes into the river.

questions.stem: Which of the following questions does the passage answer?

options.A: What finally pushed Parliament to act on the sewage problem?
options.B: Who was the first person to sell flush toilets in large numbers?
options.C: How many people died when cholera returned in 1866?
options.D: How much did it cost to build Bazalgette's sewers?

questions.stem: Based on the passage and the chart, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: By 2024, South Asia's share had climbed above the share for the world as a whole.
options.B: Sub-Saharan Africa's share more than doubled in the years between 2000 and 2024.
options.C: In 2024, the majority of people in Sub-Saharan Africa had no basic toilet of their own.
options.D: The gap between South Asia and the world grew wider in the years after 2000.

1.explanation_zh: 第一段第二句就是全文論點：聰明的發明可能在解決舊問題之前，先製造出新問題。第二段介紹抽水馬桶的發明；第三段說倫敦沒有配套的下水道時，馬桶反而讓糞坑滿溢、污物流進水井與泰晤士河；第四段說直到巴澤爾傑特建好整套下水道才扭轉局面；最後一段說今天許多地方仍缺乏基本衛生設施。(B) 用「發明要等周邊系統跟上」概括各段，是主旨。
evidence: Yet its history shows that a clever device can create a new problem long before it solves an old one.
In London, however, the new toilets at first made matters worse.

option_notes_zh.A: 與原文相反：當時的人（包括國會議員）以為疾病是經由臭氣傳播，這個想法後來證明是錯的；國會是因為怕臭氣才出錢建下水道，不是因為有人證明髒水會傳播霍亂。
option_notes_zh.C: 與原文相反：抽水馬桶剛普及時反而讓情況更糟，十九世紀倫敦有四次霍亂大流行，1866 年霍亂還再出現一次。
option_notes_zh.D: 只是第四段的細節，而且因果不完整：炎熱乾燥的夏天只是讓臭味爆發的時機，真正的原因是污物被排進泰晤士河。

A: Like most people of their time, they believed that diseases spread through bad air rather than dirty water.
C: In London, however, the new toilets at first made matters worse.

1.strategy_zh: 主旨題先找作者明說論點的句子（本文在第一段末），再檢查選項能否涵蓋各段；只抓到一段細節的（D），或和原文因果相反的（A）（C），都不是主旨。
hints: 第一段第二句說，抽水馬桶的歷史顯示了什麼？
第三段說馬桶剛出現時，對倫敦是幫助還是麻煩？第四段的下水道又解決了什麼？
找一個能把「發明」和「配套系統」連起來、而且不違反文意的選項。

2.explanation_zh: 1847 年起，糞坑「必須」接上公共下水道；但這些下水道原本是為排雨水而建，直接排進泰晤士河。也就是說，原本積在房子底下的污物，改為流進河裡——所以 1858 年才會出現臭氣沖天的「大惡臭」。(D) 是把第三段兩句接起來、再對照第四段推得的結論。
evidence: In 1815 the city first allowed cesspools to be connected to the public sewers, and in 1847 such connections became compulsory.
But those sewers had been built to carry rainwater, and they emptied straight into the Thames.

option_notes_zh.A: 與原文相反：十九世紀倫敦共有四次霍亂大流行，1866 年霍亂還再出現，1847 年的法律並沒有終結霍亂。
option_notes_zh.B: 時間錯置：大惡臭發生在 1858 年，比 1847 年晚了十一年；因大惡臭而通過的，是讓巴澤爾傑特興建下水道的另一項法律。
option_notes_zh.C: 細節錯置：1847 年規定的是糞坑必須接上公共下水道，不是每戶都要裝抽水馬桶。

A: When cholera returned in 1866, it struck only a district in the east where the system was not yet complete.
B: The turning point came in the hot, dry summer of 1858, when the river smelled so foul that the period became known as the Great Stink.
C: In 1815 the city first allowed cesspools to be connected to the public sewers, and in 1847 such connections became compulsory.

2.strategy_zh: 推論題要把相鄰句子接起來：「必須接上下水道」＋「下水道直通泰晤士河」→ 污物進了河。再用年份（1847 對 1858）排除倒因為果的選項。
hints: 1847 年規定了什麼事情「必須」做？
那些下水道原本是做什麼用的？最後把東西排到哪裡？
污物原本在哪裡、後來到了哪裡？注意大惡臭發生在 1847 年之後。

3.explanation_zh: 第四段說 1858 年夏天泰晤士河臭到國會議員在河邊的房間裡待不下去；他們以為疾病靠臭氣傳播，出於恐懼才採取行動，通過法律讓巴澤爾傑特開始興建下水道。所以「是什麼終於促使國會處理污水問題」在文中有答案。
evidence: Members of Parliament could barely stay in their rooms beside the water.
They were wrong, but their fear made them act.

option_notes_zh.B: 看似有答案：文中只說布拉馬到 1797 年已賣出六千多個，並沒有說他是「第一個」大量販售的人。
option_notes_zh.C: 看似有答案：文中提到 1866 年霍亂再起，但沒有說那一次的死亡人數；近四萬人是整個十九世紀四次流行的總數。
option_notes_zh.D: 文中沒有提到下水道的造價。

C: Over the century, four outbreaks of cholera killed almost 40,000 Londoners.

3.strategy_zh: 「文中能回答哪個問題」要逐一核對：看似有答案的選項常差一個關鍵詞（「第一個」、「那一次」的死亡人數），文中沒有剛好對應的資訊就不能選。
hints: (B) 問「第一個」大量販售的人：文中有說誰是第一個嗎？
(C) 問 1866 年那一次的死亡人數：40,000 指的是哪一段期間的總數？
第四段說國會為什麼「終於」行動？

4.explanation_zh: 文中把「基本衛生設施」定義為合格、而且不與其他家戶共用的廁所。圖表中 2024 年 Sub-Saharan Africa 只有 37.1% 的人有這樣的廁所，也就是約六成三的人沒有，所以「2024 年 Sub-Saharan Africa 過半數的人沒有自家可用的合格廁所」正確。
evidence: The chart below shows the share of people using at least basic sanitation, meaning a properly built toilet that is not shared with other households.
2024, Sub-Saharan Africa: 37.1%

option_notes_zh.A: 數字很接近但不正確：2024 年 South Asia 是 82.0%，World 是 82.2%，仍略低於全球。
option_notes_zh.B: 計算錯誤：21.9% 到 37.1% 只增加約七成，沒有翻倍；增加超過一倍的是 South Asia。
option_notes_zh.D: 與圖表相反：2000 年兩者相差 38.2 個百分點，2024 年只差 0.2，差距是縮小。

4.strategy_zh: 圖文整合題先確認縱軸數字的意義（本題要用文中的定義換算「沒有」的人），再逐一驗算：「超過」要比 82.0 和 82.2；「翻倍」要用除法；「差距」要算兩個年份的差。
hints: 縱軸的百分比是「有」還是「沒有」基本衛生設施的人？
2024 年 Sub-Saharan Africa 是多少？沒有的人大約占幾成？
逐一驗算：82.0 和 82.2 哪個大？21.9 到 37.1 有沒有翻倍？兩個年份的差距變大還是變小？

translation_zh.text:
很少有發明像抽水馬桶這樣容易被忽略。然而它的歷史顯示，一項巧妙的裝置可能早在解決舊問題之前，就先製造出新的問題。
1590 年代，英國朝臣約翰・哈靈頓爵士描述了一種用水把穢物沖走的座便器，並為伊莉莎白一世女王造了一座。將近兩百年後的 1775 年，一位名叫亞歷山大・康明的蘇格蘭鐘錶匠，以管子上有 S 形彎道的設計取得專利。留在彎道裡的水能封住從排水管冒上來的臭味——馬桶至今仍仰賴這項設計。1778 年，約瑟夫・布拉馬為一款以把手操作的改良型取得專利，到 1797 年已賣出六千多座。
然而在倫敦，新式馬桶起初反而讓情況更糟。每沖一次水，就有兩加侖以上的水流進糞坑——也就是房子底下長久以來收集穢物的坑。糞坑很快就滿了、開始滲漏，穢物滲進供應飲用水的水井。1815 年，倫敦首度允許糞坑接上公共下水道；1847 年起，這樣的連接成為強制規定。但那些下水道原本是為排放雨水而建，直接流進泰晤士河。整個十九世紀，四次霍亂大流行奪走了將近四萬名倫敦人的性命。
轉捩點出現在 1858 年炎熱乾燥的夏天：河水臭得驚人，那段時期因此被稱為「大惡臭」。國會議員幾乎無法待在河邊的辦公室裡。和當時大多數人一樣，他們相信疾病是透過污濁的空氣、而不是髒水傳播。他們錯了，但恐懼讓他們採取了行動。國會很快通過法律，讓工程師約瑟夫・巴澤爾傑特在 1859 年 1 月開始興建龐大的下水道網。沿著河岸延伸的巨大隧道攔截污水，把它往東送離市中心。1866 年霍亂再度來襲時，只侵襲了東邊一個系統尚未完工的地區。
巴澤爾傑特處理的問題，並沒有在每個地方都消失。下圖顯示使用至少基本衛生設施的人口比例——所謂基本衛生設施，是指合格、而且不與其他家戶共用的廁所。聯合國每年 11 月 19 日訂為世界廁所日，並非偶然。
【圖】使用至少基本衛生設施的人口比例（%），2000–2024 年。

open_tasks.prompt: Bazalgette solved London's problem with a huge sewer system. Do you think the same solution would work for places where most people still lack a basic toilet today? Answer in 1–2 English sentences and give a reason.
reference_answers: Not always, because building huge sewers costs a lot of money and time, so simpler toilets that keep waste away from drinking water may help people sooner.
Yes, in big cities it could work, because a sewer system protects the water supply for everyone, just as it did in London.

有沒有說出理由（成本、時間、保護水源等）
有沒有用到文中或圖表的資訊

Each flush sent two gallons or more of water into cesspools beneath houses; they filled quickly, leaked, and waste seeped into wells.（f8–f10；Gresham 講稿：two gallons or more of water, rapidly filling the cesspools…which leaked；springs and wells from which drinking water was drawn）
In 1815 the city first allowed cesspools to be connected to the public sewers; in 1847 such connections became compulsory.（f12；講稿原文一致）

The sewers had been built to carry rainwater and emptied into the Thames.（f11、f13；講稿：Public sewers…were for disposing of rainwater；carried their contents into underground rivers and thence into the Thames——文中 straight 是簡化，核心事實一致）
Over the century, four outbreaks of cholera killed almost 40,000 Londoners.（f15；講稿：In London alone in the nineteenth century almost 40,000 people died in four cholera epidemics）
The hot, dry summer of 1858 brought the Great Stink; MPs could barely stay in their rooms beside the river.（f17；講稿：hot, dry summer；Committee Rooms and the Library were utterly unable to remain there）
Like most people of their time, MPs believed diseases spread through bad air rather than dirty water, which was wrong.（f16；講稿：miasmatic theory…later revealed as mistaken）
Parliament passed a law letting Bazalgette begin building sewers in January 1859.（f18；講稿：a Bill…authorised Bazalgette to start work immediately；Work began in January 1859）
Huge tunnels alongside the river caught the waste and carried it east.（f19；講稿：intercepting sewers running parallel to the river；outfalls at Beckton and Crossness）

When cholera returned in 1866, it struck only a district in the east where the system was not yet complete.（f20；講稿：summer of 1866…one square mile of Whitechapel…the only part of Bazalgette's system that was not complete）
The United Nations marks World Toilet Day every year on 19 November.（f21；UN 原頁一致）
Basic sanitation means a properly built toilet not shared with other households.（f23；World Bank SH.STA.BASS.ZS 定義）
